title: Bound label scan image resources
scope: Assigned security repair: bound actual photo download bytes, image pixels and aggregate session scan resources; prepare crops one photo at a time rather than retaining all oriented photos; share a process-wide nonqueued scan slot across photo and session endpoints; preserve authorization, crop coordinates, AI batching and persistence. No upload or UI changes.
why: Backend image processing and route integration require unit regression coverage plus compiler checks.
coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-standard typecheck and unit-tests run server/__tests__/routes.test.ts including the image resource boundary tests; existing lint and runtime contracts remain included.

approval.reference: Assigned task 993 in the active conversation
approval.direction: Patch resource exhaustion in session label scanning without new product flows
approval.applicability: Security hardening and regression coverage within assigned scope; no independent verification selected

assertions.check: Stream readers reject actual bytes exceeding the remaining budget and destroy the stream, including missing or inaccurate metadata.
Real Sharp fixtures reject excessive dimensions, aggregate pixels and bytes before provider work; ordinary oriented crops retain order and dimensions.

Production scan preparation loads one photo at a time, ignores foreign-session photos, and rejects over-budget scans; shared slot rejects overlap and releases idempotently after errors. Both routes use the protected preparation and release slot in finally.

regression.rationale: Repairs authenticated denial of service through unbounded retained images and overlapping native processing.
regression.covers: R1 unbounded photo reads; R2 decompression and aggregate scan memory; R3 concurrent scans and resource leaks
regression.assertion: Bounded stream fixtures assert rejection and destruction, Sharp image fixtures assert early pixel and aggregate budget failures, production preparation fixtures assert crop ordering and foreign-session exclusion, and slot fixtures assert overlap rejection and release on failure. Route wiring assertions cover both protected endpoints.
